skill.name: ball-ranks
skill.description: Get published Ball Ranks fantasy basketball and football rankings and player projections through its read-only MCP server or REST API. Use for draft boards, player comparisons, and football weekly start/sit questions grounded in Ball Ranks data.
skill.summary: Compare fantasy basketball and football players using published Ball Ranks rankings, projections, and source links.
skill.author: ollynov

The skill limits credentials to Ball Ranks requests and describes read-only data access. No evidence found of prompt injection, unauthorized data exfiltration, or system reconnaissance; the remote service implementation was not available for review.

content.user_title: Compare Fantasy Players with Ball Ranks
content.value_statement: Fantasy player comparisons need rankings that match the sport, scoring format, and time period. This skill retrieves published Ball Ranks data and cites its source.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve published basketball and football season ranking boards through MCP tools or read-only REST requests.
Look up an individual player's season rank and published projections using a known Ball Ranks identifier.
Retrieve football weekly position rankings and weekly player projections for supported weeks.
Compare players using matching sport, model, season, scope, and football scoring settings.
Cite returned source links and identify the data model, season, week, and available freshness metadata.
Handle authorization failures, unavailable data, unsupported requests, and shared REST and MCP rate limits.
limitations: Requires access to the external Ball Ranks service through an MCP client or REST-capable tool; no offline dataset is included.
Basketball season rankings use nine-category per-game scoring; weekly scopes apply only to football.
Model One requires an authorized Premium account key; anonymous access uses Model Zero.
Only currently published seasons and available player data are supported; quotas and service outages can prevent retrieval.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Basketball Draft Board
use_cases.description: Retrieve a season board and review nine-category per-game ranks with player projections and source links.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Weekly Football Starters
use_cases.description: Compare players at the same position using weekly rankings and projections for the league's scoring format.

use_cases.title: Research Published Player Comparisons
use_cases.description: Summarize player rankings and projections while documenting the model, season, scope, source, and available update time.

prompt_templates.title: View a Season Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the top 10 fantasy basketball players in the current published Ball Ranks Model Zero season rankings. Include scoring context and source links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve a small ranking board.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Player Projection
prompt_templates.prompt: Get Victor Wembanyama's Model Zero basketball season projection using his Ball Ranks identifier. Report available stats, season, source, and update time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: retrieve one player's published projection.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Weekly Football Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [player A] and [player B] for week [week] at [position] in half-PPR football. Use Model Zero weekly rankings and projections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate a weekly lineup decision.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Consistent Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [players] using current published PPR football season rankings and projections. Use authorized Model One access; otherwise ask before falling back to Model Zero. Use known player IDs, minimize requests, cite sources, preserve missing values, and separate your recommendation from published data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage model access and data consistency across several players.

output_examples.input: Compare these two football receivers for week 4, but I have not specified league scoring.
output_examples.output: Which scoring format does your league use: standard, half-PPR, or PPR?
Ball Ranks weekly rankings apply to football only. Basketball season rankings use nine-category per-game scoring.

output_examples.input: Report a player projection when the service returns no published data.
output_examples.output: No published projection was returned for this request. I cannot provide a Ball Ranks projection without available source data.

best_practices: Specify sport, scoring format, position, and week when relevant; compare players using the same model and scope.
Use one ranking board when possible, fetch the smallest useful page, and respect shared service quotas.
Cite source links, preserve missing values, and keep API keys out of URLs, logs, answers, and committed files.
anti_patterns: Compare players across different scoring formats, models, seasons, or ranking scopes without explaining the differences.
Invent rankings, treat missing values as zero, or present an unavailable projection as published data.
Retry exhausted quotas repeatedly or switch from Model One to Model Zero without user acceptance.

faq.question: Which sports does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports published Ball Ranks fantasy basketball and football rankings and player projections.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Anonymous requests use Model Zero. Model One requires a user-supplied key belonging to a Premium account and explicit authorization.

faq.question: Can it work without an MCP connection?
faq.answer: Yes, when your assistant has a REST-capable tool. The skill documents read-only REST requests as an alternative.

faq.question: Which scoring formats are supported?
faq.answer: Football supports standard, half-PPR, and PPR. Basketball season rankings use nine-category per-game scoring.

faq.question: Can it retrieve weekly basketball or historical rankings?
faq.answer: Weekly scopes apply only to football. Explicit season requests must match currently published data; unrestricted historical access is not documented.

faq.question: How does it handle limits and missing data?
faq.answer: It respects shared REST and MCP quotas and retry headers. It reports unavailable data instead of inventing rankings or projections.
